newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $68 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $68 - trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Wednesday were slow, with not enough confirmed sales for an adequate market test, according to feedlot sources.
About 500 head sold in Kansas and an estimated 2,000 sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area at $68.00 per cwt, unchanged with Tuesday's active sales.
Sales were light because many packers reportedly bought enough cattle during Tuesday's brisk activity to get them into early next week, the feedlot sources said.
Near 63,000 head were estimated near midday in the Panhandle for the week to date including 14,000 formulated and 2,300 previously contracted cattle to be shipped this week, according to USDA.
In Kansas, 68,400 head were projected for the week including 26,500 head or about 39 percent previously contracted or formulated cattle, USDA said.
Most feedlots were asking $68.00 to $70.00 for the cattle remaining on this week's showlists, which some feedlot sources said could use a few extra days on feed.
